correctness.rationale: Necessity follows because two omitted vertices in one peripheral clique have identical distances to every landmark. For sufficiency, the proof exhausts the three pair types: same blade, different blades, and center versus blade, and explicitly exhibits two landmarks with different distance differences in each case. The factorized polynomial then follows from independent per-blade choices and the optional center. An exhaustive checker independently confirms the criterion and coefficients for eight small parameter pairs up to order 13 and checks both excluded boundaries.

originality.rationale: The closest literature supplies the definition, a twin-set necessity lemma, or results for different graph families/parameters. None of the inspected sources states the generalized-windmill if-and-only-if characterization, its full polynomial, or the exact basis multiplicity. The new claim is not a special case of the closest chain-graph or complete-multipartite results.
residual_risks: A doubly-resolving windmill result could exist in unindexed literature or under notation not reached by the searched aliases.

The 2023 twin-set lemma is a prior ingredient for necessity, so originality rests specifically on the converse, all-set characterization, and exact enumerator rather than on the twin lower bound itself.

value.rationale: Generalized windmills are a canonical clique-sum family and include all friendship graphs. The result gives more than a scalar invariant: it classifies every doubly resolving set and yields the full cardinality polynomial, minimum value, and exact basis multiplicity in one factorized formula. Doubly resolving sets are directly tied to Cartesian-product metric dimension in the foundational literature, so this all-set structure is a natural reusable exact fact rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
